mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes slime moulds?

options.C: They are eukaryotic organisms that can exist as single cells and aggregate to form multicellular fruiting bodies.

mcqs.answer: They are eukaryotic organisms that can exist as single cells and aggregate to form multicellular fruiting bodies.
mcqs.explanation: Slime moulds belong to the kingdom Protista. They live as individual amoeboid cells when food is abundant, but under starvation they aggregate to form a multicellular, spore‑bearing structure. They are not plants, fungi, or bacteria.

mcqs.question: Protozoans are best characterized by which feature?

options.C: Being unicellular eukaryotes that show animal‑like movement and ingest food.
options.D: Having cell walls made of cellulose.

mcqs.answer: Being unicellular eukaryotes that show animal‑like movement and ingest food.
mcqs.explanation: Protozoans are animal‑like protists. They are single‑celled, lack cell walls, move by flagella, cilia or pseudopodia, and obtain nutrients by phagocytosis or absorption. They are not photosynthetic, multicellular, nor do they have cellulose walls.

mcqs.question: Which of the following distinguishes members of the kingdom Protista from plants, animals and fungi?

options.A: They are all multicellular and have cell walls of chitin.
options.C: They are primarily unicellular eukaryotes with diverse modes of nutrition and locomotion.

mcqs.answer: They are primarily unicellular eukaryotes with diverse modes of nutrition and locomotion.
mcqs.explanation: Protists are mostly single‑celled eukaryotes. Unlike plants, animals and fungi, they exhibit a wide range of nutritional strategies (photosynthetic, heterotrophic, mixotrophic) and movement mechanisms (flagella, cilia, pseudopodia). They possess a true nucleus, unlike prokaryotes.

mcqs.question: Which major protist group includes organisms that are primarily photosynthetic and possess chlorophyll a and c, such as diatoms?
mcqs.explanation: Diatoms belong to the algal group Bacillariophyta. They are photosynthetic protists that contain chlorophyll a and c and have siliceous cell walls. Protozoa are animal‑like, Myxomycetes are slime moulds, and Euglenoids are a different photosynthetic/heterotrophic group.

mcqs.question: Chrysophytes are best recognized by which characteristic?

options.A: They are non‑photosynthetic parasites of higher plants.
options.B: They have golden‑brown pigments and produce siliceous scales or cysts.
options.C: They are flagellated heterotrophs lacking chloroplasts.
options.D: They form large multicellular fruiting bodies on land.

mcqs.answer: They have golden‑brown pigments and produce siliceous scales or cysts.
mcqs.explanation: Chrysophytes (golden algae) contain fucoxanthin, giving them a golden‑brown colour, and many produce siliceous scales or cysts. They are photosynthetic, not parasitic, and they are unicellular, not large fruiting bodies.

mcqs.question: A marine biologist observes a red tide caused by a bloom of organisms that are bioluminescent, have two flagella arranged perpendicular to each other, and possess cellulose plates. Which group do these organisms belong to?
mcqs.explanation: Dinoflagellates have two flagella (one transverse, one longitudinal) and cellulose plates called theca. Many are bioluminescent and cause red tides. Diatoms have a single girdle of silica, euglenoids have a single flagellum, and cyanobacteria are prokaryotes.

mcqs.question: Which statement about euglenoids is correct?

options.A: They are true plants because they have chloroplasts and cell walls of cellulose.
options.B: They are animal‑like protists that never contain chloroplasts.
options.C: They are photosynthetic protists that can also ingest food in the absence of light.
options.D: They are multicellular algae found only in marine environments.

mcqs.answer: They are photosynthetic protists that can also ingest food in the absence of light.
mcqs.explanation: Euglenoids possess chloroplasts and can photosynthesize, but they also have a pellicle and can feed heterotrophically by phagocytosis when light is scarce. They are not true plants (lack cellulose cell walls) and are unicellular, not multicellular marine algae.

mcqs.question: If a slime mould is placed on a moist agar plate that contains a lawn of bacteria, what is the most likely behaviour of the slime mould?

options.A: It will produce spores immediately without feeding.
options.B: It will remain dormant as a cyst.
options.C: It will form a migrating plasmodium that engulfs the bacteria.
options.D: It will convert into a photosynthetic organism.

mcqs.answer: It will form a migrating plasmodium that engulfs the bacteria.
mcqs.explanation: When food (bacteria) is available, slime moulds aggregate to form a motile plasmodium that moves over the substrate, feeding by phagocytosing bacteria. They do not produce spores instantly, nor do they become photosynthetic, and they are active rather than dormant in the presence of food.
